claims.claim: Every claim has assumptions, definitions, mechanisms, tests, limits, consequences, and failure conditions that can be systematically exposed.
claims.plain_english: Any statement you make depends on hidden ideas about how the world works, and you can find them all by asking the right questions.
claims.evidence_given: The document presents the 7Q method as a repeatable classifier and claims it makes claims 'inspectable' by turning them around until every load-bearing surface is visible.
claims.what_would_break_it: If there existed a claim that had no underlying assumptions or that could not be decomposed into these seven categories, the claim would be false.

claims.claim: The 7Q method makes inquiry repeatable by naming the roots of a claim.
claims.plain_english: If you use the seven questions, anyone can check your reasoning the same way every time.
claims.evidence_given: The document asserts this as the purpose of the method and provides the seven question labels (Q1–Q7) but does not demonstrate the method on a concrete example.
claims.what_would_break_it: If two different people applying the 7Q method to the same claim arrived at fundamentally different root structures, the method would not be repeatable.

claims.claim: The 7Q method is a machine, not a slogan.
claims.plain_english: The seven questions work like a reliable tool, not just a catchy idea.
claims.evidence_given: The document states this as a conclusion but provides no empirical test or demonstration of the method's reliability.
claims.what_would_break_it: If applying the 7Q method produced inconsistent or contradictory results across different users or contexts, it would be a slogan, not a machine.

claims.plain_english: Using the seven questions prevents you from fooling yourself or others about what your claim really means.
claims.evidence_given: The document claims the method 'keeps the method stages visible' and that the instrument keeps conclusions honest, but no empirical evidence is provided.
claims.what_would_break_it: If someone could use the 7Q method to justify a false claim as easily as a true one, the method would not keep conclusions honest.

claims.claim: The goal of the 7Q method is to make every claim inspectable, not to make every claim sound smart.
claims.plain_english: The point is to let anyone check your claim, not to make it look impressive.
claims.evidence_given: The document explicitly states this as the goal and contrasts it with making claims sound smart.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the method were used primarily to make claims appear more rigorous without actually enabling independent verification, the goal would be contradicted.

claims.claim: The 7Q method can be applied to any claim across domains (physics, theology, math, morality).
claims.plain_english: You can use these seven questions on any kind of statement, whether it's about science, God, numbers, or right and wrong.
claims.evidence_given: The document is part of a series titled 'Faith Through Physics' and mentions bridging domains, but does not demonstrate the method on a claim from theology or morality.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a claim from theology or morality could not be decomposed into the seven categories without losing its essential meaning, the method would not be domain-independent.

claims.claim: The 7Q method turns a claim around until every load-bearing surface is visible.
claims.plain_english: The method forces you to look at every part of a claim that supports it, like checking every beam in a building.
claims.evidence_given: The document uses the metaphor of load-bearing surfaces and states the method 'refuses to hide the structure,' but provides no worked example.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a claim had hidden assumptions that the 7Q method systematically missed, the method would not make all load-bearing surfaces visible.
